ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a grid composed of 1 cm × 1 cm small squares, which as a whole can be read as a rectangle of 9 columns and 3 rows. The shaded figure is located within this 9×3 rectangle, and the boundary has several slanted lines, with the endpoints of the slanted lines all falling on grid intersections. The unshaded part can be divided into several triangular regions. Reasoning: The area of the entire 9×3 rectangle is 9×3=27 cm². By the complement method, subtract the unshaded regions from the whole rectangle: the left triangle has base 2 and height 3, with area 1/2×2×3=3; the middle small V-shaped triangle has base 2 and height 1, with area 1; the area of the triangle below from the bottom point of the 4th column to the point in the 1st row of the 6th column is 2; the area of the triangle below from the point in the 1st row of the 6th column to the bottom point of the 7th column is 1; the right triangle has base 2 and height 3, with area 3. The total unshaded area is 3+1+2+1+3=10 cm². Therefore the shaded area is 27−10=17 cm².

From the image, read the full grid as a 9-by-3 rectangle and note that the shaded polygon lies inside it, with slanted edges hitting grid intersections. The whole rectangle has area 27 square units. Subtract the unshaded white regions: the left triangle with base 2 and height 3 has area 3; the small central V-shaped triangle with base 2 and height 1 has area 1; the triangle under the segment from the bottom point at column 4 to the point at column 6,row 1 has area 2; the triangle under the segment from column 6,row 1 to column 7,bottom has area 1; and the right triangle with base 2 and height 3 has area 3. The total unshaded area is 10, so the shaded area is 27-10=17 square units. Since each grid square is 1 cm by 1 cm, the area is 17 cm^2.
